jurisdiction_name: United States (federal, applies in all states)
requirement_summary: Determine estimated location of utility installations and contact utility owners before excavating; protective systems required for excavations 5 ft or deeper unless in stable rock.

Emergency excavations are exempt from the notice time requirements when delay would cause imminent risk to life, health, or property; notice of emergency excavation is still required. Owner must attempt to contact the excavator within 1 hour and arrive within 2 hours to locate and mark (Idaho Code 55-2205(4)).

jurisdiction_name: United States (federal, applies in all states)
requirement_summary: Direct notice of planned copper retirement at least 90 days before implementation (at least 15 days if the copper serves no customers) to directly interconnected telephone exchange service providers, 911 service providers and interconnecting LECs supporting 911; public notice via industry fora/publications or ILEC website (FCC filing eliminated).

jurisdiction_name: United States (federal, applies in all states)
requirement_summary: Section 214(a) authorization required to discontinue, reduce or impair service. Application automatically granted on the 31st day after filing for all domestic carriers unless FCC notifies otherwise; customer objections due no later than 15 days after FCC public notice.

jurisdiction_name: United States (federal, applies in all states)
requirement_summary: At least 90-day pre-filing 911 coordination notice for discontinuances affecting 911 facilities.

jurisdiction_name: United States (federal, applies in all states)
requirement_summary: Wastes leaching lead at or above 5.0 mg/L by TCLP are D008 hazardous waste under RCRA Subtitle C (lead-sheathed cable, contaminated soil).

Written notice at least 30 days before ceasing any telecom service to the UTC, state 911 program, each customer, ILECs providing UNEs, resale providers and the number administrator. Does NOT apply when the provider replaces the service with comparable service without interruption (WAC 480-120-083(1)(c)).

To discontinue basic emergency service, switched access, service required for basic emergency service, or basic local exchange service provided by an ETC or EP, file an application not less than 45 days before the proposed effective date.

Customer transition plan petition to the PUC (alternative providers required). Approval requires a public meeting in the affected area with written notice to customers 60 days in advance; disputes submitted at least 90 days before discontinuance and resolved 15 days before. Effective 2026-07-01.

90 days notice to customers and the PUC before a certificated provider with Oregon customers may have its certificate cancelled (also for transfers). This is certificate cancellation, not a copper-retirement-specific rule.
citation: ORS 759.506; Oregon PUC certificate cancellation/transfer notice (OAR 860 Div. 32 referenced)

requirement_summary: A company ceasing service where it is the only ETC must petition the Commission at least 90 days before intended termination; deemed granted if not denied or set for hearing within 90 days.

Federal Section 214 discontinuance authorization applies (47 CFR 63.71, 31-day auto-grant). State discontinuance rules are separate (see state_discontinuance_notice). FCC 26-19 says state mandates conflicting with FCC 214 authorizations are subject to preemption.

2 to 10 full business days before work-to-begin date (RCW 19.122.030(2)).
Marks expire 45 calendar days from notice date, or duration of excavation if shorter (RCW 19.122.030(6)).
Markings valid 15 working days from marking; request extension at least 2 working days before end of validity (A.R.S. 40-360.22(J)).

Notify the notification association before excavating (9-1.5-102(2)(a), 103(3)); owner/operator marks within 2 business days not counting the notice day (103(4)(a)(I)). Minimum excavator advance-notice period not separately stated in verified excerpt.
Markings within 18 inches horizontally of the facility exterior sides (C.R.S. 9-1.5-103(4)(a)(I)).
Valid while visible but not more than 30 calendar days after the locate request due date (C.R.S. 9-1.5-103(4)(b)).
At least 48 hours (excluding notice day, Saturdays, Sundays, holidays) and not more than 14 calendar days before excavation (216D.04 subd. 1(a)).
Excavator must determine precise location before excavating within 2 feet on either side of the marked location (216D.04 subd. 4(a)).
Notice valid 14 calendar days from start time; continuing work requires new notice at least 48 hours before expiration (216D.04 subd. 4(c)).
Notify OUNC at least 2 but not more than 10 business days before excavation (ORS 757.557(2), statute text verified).
Notice not less than 2 nor more than 10 business days before excavation (Idaho Code 55-2205(1)).
Markings valid no longer than 4 consecutive weeks following notification unless agreed in writing (Idaho Code 55-2205).

Cities/towns may require a master permit (act on complete application within 120 days) and use permits (act within 30 days); may not unreasonably deny ROW use to install, maintain, repair or remove telecom facilities.

requirement_summary: OSHA lead-in-construction standard applies where employees may be exposed to lead, including demolition/salvage and removal of lead-containing materials (lead-sheathed cable harvesting).

Yes: one-call center provides an interactive positive response system; operator notifies excavator via it when marking is unnecessary (A.R.S. 40-360.22(B),(V)).
Required: before submitting a location request the excavator must mark the excavation area with white lining (A.R.S. 40-360.22(C)); exception for certain single-family residential excavations.
Yes: positive response documentation via the notification association required, including no-facility responses (C.R.S. 9-1.5-103(4),(6.5)).
Emergency situations (ruptures, leaks, explosions, fires and similar where immediate action is needed and advance notice is impracticable) are excepted from the notify-before-excavating requirement.
The 48-hour advance notice requirement applies "except in an emergency".

ADOT Director has complete and exclusive operational control and jurisdiction over use of state highways (A.R.S. 28-7045). ADOT encroachment permit rule A.A.C. R17-3-502 is UNVERIFIED (official PDF blocked).

Authorized telecom/broadband providers may construct, maintain and operate facilities along, across, upon, above and under any public highway, subject to C.R.S. 38-5.5 and the one-call law; ROW across state land requires just compensation and State Land Board conditions.
Local governments manage public ROW and issue permits for telecom ROW users (Minn. Stat. 237.162-237.163); MnDOT Utility Accommodation Policy applies on trunk highways.
No person may place cable or other facilities on state highway or county road ROW without written permission from ODOT (state highways) or the county (county roads); violation is a misdemeanor.
Idaho Transportation Department permits utility installations within state highway ROW.
RCW 19.122.030(1)(a): before commencing excavation the excavator must mark the boundary with white lining or white pin flags. White lining defined in RCW 19.122.020. Mandatory (not conditional).

RCW 19.122.031(1)(a): emergency excavation exempt from white lining and notice requirements of RCW 19.122.030(1) and (2), provided excavator gives notice to a one-number locator service at the earliest practicable time. Emergency defined in RCW 19.122.020(7).

C.R.S. 9-1.5-103(3)(c)(II): if an area of excavation cannot be accurately described, the excavator shall delineate using physical marking (white paint/stakes/flags), electronic means, or on-site meeting. CONDITIONAL — not a universal pre-mark mandate.

Minn. Stat. 216D.05(a)(2): for proposed excavations the excavator must use white markings (or black in wintery conditions), or electronic marking. 216D.04 subd. 1b(c): for on-site meets the excavator must mark the boundary.

NOT_REQUIRED_BY_STATUTE: full text of Minn. Stat. ch. 216D scanned 2026-10-25 — zero matches for "positive response". The operator response duty is in 216D.04 subd. 3(a),(e) but no statutory positive-response tracking system.

Idaho Code 55-2205(1)(b): before commencing excavation the excavator shall pre-mark on-site the path of excavation with white paint or other reasonable means. Exceptions: owner can determine location by street address or other description.
NOT_REQUIRED_BY_STATUTE: Idaho Code 55-2205 text scanned for "positive response" — zero matches. No statutory positive-response system. Response duty is in 55-2205(2) but no tracking requirement.

requirement_summary: OAR 952-001-0010(23) ticket life changed from 45 days to 30 days, effective January 8, 2026 (2026 Addendum to Oregon Standards Manual). Resolves prior conflict between 45-day compilation and OUNC announcement.

OAR 952-001-0010(7) defines emergency as occurrence involving immediate danger demanding urgent action. OAR 952-001-0060 allows emergency locates. OUNC FAQ: call 811 for emergency locate, report damage.

Lead-bearing waste (e.g. lead-sheathed cable, contaminated soil) at or above 5.0 mg/L lead by TCLP is dangerous waste D008 (WAC 173-303-090). Excluded scrap metal being recycled is excluded from dangerous waste rules (WAC 173-303-071(3)(ff)). Worker exposure: WA DOSH construction lead standard WAC 296-155-176 et seq. (WA runs an OSHA State Plan). No telecom-cable-specific state rule found (verified absence per @data-planner ACC-DP-LEAD-STATE-RULES); state relies on general hazardous-waste toxicity and scrap-metal recycling rules. Confirm handling with counsel.

Oregon DEQ hazardous waste rules adopt the federal RCRA rules in 40 CFR 261 by reference, so the D008 lead toxicity characteristic (5.0 mg/L TCLP) and the federal recycled scrap-metal exclusion apply. Worker exposure: Oregon OSHA Division 3 adopts 29 CFR 1926.62 plus OAR 437-003-0062 (lead respiratory protection program); Oregon runs an OSHA State Plan. Exact OAR 340-100/-101 section numbers not verified. No telecom-cable-specific state rule found (verified absence per @data-planner ACC-DP-LEAD-STATE-RULES); state relies on general hazardous-waste toxicity and scrap-metal recycling rules. Confirm handling with counsel.
citation: OAR ch. 340 div. 100-102 (adopts 40 CFR 261); Oregon OSHA Div. 3 (29 CFR 1926.62, OAR 437-003-0062)

requirement_summary: Waste at or above 5.0 mg/L lead by TCLP is hazardous (D008) under Minn. R. 7045.0131. Recycled scrap metal is not subject to Minn. R. 7045.0205 to 7045.0695 (Minn. R. 7045.0125, subp. 4(C)). Worker exposure: MNOSHA adopts 29 CFR Part 1926 incl. 1926.62 (Minn. R. 5205.0010, subp. 6); Minnesota runs an OSHA State Plan. requirement_summary: A.R.S. 40-360.28(F)(1): the civil-penalty and liability section does not apply to an excavation made during an emergency that involves immediate danger to life, health or property, if reasonable precautions are taken to protect underground facilities. A.R.S. 40-360.24 requires notice to 911 or the local emergency response agency on a damage or release. Art. 6.3 sets no separate emergency-locate ticket procedure; Arizona 811 operating procedures for emergency tickets are not yet sourced.
